metadata.description: Proposed Solid Carbon monitoring tools. Each hole is a point. Planned equipment is placed from the site-layout slides: the distance is the one written on the slide and the direction is the one drawn on it (mini junction box ~15–20 m NE, sonar 20–30 m NW, hydrophone array 3–5 m from Bay A, camera 3–5 m from the pump). Where a slide gives no distance (injection pump, 1026B camera) about 3 m is used. Tether and cable lines are schematic, not surveyed routes. Items mounted on a CORK (on_cork) are drawn at 75% size, about 0.86 m from the hole, spaced so that at the map's closest zoom (22) no two are within the 30 px grouping radius; OSMO-samplers and pressure sensors are already installed, the Ferry Box is planned.

properties.name: U1362A
properties.connection: To be cabled to ONC via 1026B (≈235 m)
instruments: "Ferry Box" with fluorometer, "carbon" meter and resistivity meter (CTD)

properties.name: 1026B
instruments: "Ferry Box" with fluorometer, "carbon" meter and resistivity meter (CTD)

properties.name: U1362B
properties.connection: Autonomous; cable connection possible (≈311 m from U1362A)

properties.name: Mini junction box
properties.note: About 15–20 m NE of CORK A; the cable continues 235 m NE to the 1026 IP
properties.description: A small local hub that gives the planned instruments power and communications and links them to the cable.

properties.name: Sonar (COVIS)
properties.note: 20–30 m NW of CORK A, from the wall between Bays B and C, opposite the hydrophones
properties.description: An imaging sonar that scans the surrounding water and seafloor with sound, to detect fluids rising from the seafloor and changes around the site.

properties.name: Camera with pan & tilt
properties.note: 3–5 m from the injection pump in Bay C
properties.description: A camera on a motorised mount that swivels up, down and sideways, to watch the injection site and the other equipment.

properties.name: CO2 injection pump
properties.note: Injection pump for Bay C ("Lateral" or top plug), in view of the camera; the slide gives no distance
properties.description: Pumps CO₂-charged fluid down the borehole into the basalt beneath the seafloor, where the carbon is meant to turn into solid mineral.

properties.name: Hydrophone array (4, high-frequency)
properties.note: 3–5 m from Bay A, opposite the future sonar
properties.description: Four high-frequency hydrophones (underwater microphones) that listen around the site and can help locate where sounds come from.

properties.name: Camera (no pan & tilt)
properties.note: Against the east side of CORK 1026B; the slide gives no distance
properties.description: A fixed camera that films the equipment at the borehole.

properties.name: Pressure sensor
properties.note: Mounted on the CORK wellhead (Pressure Monitoring Bay A)
properties.description: Logs the pressure of the fluid in the borehole, which responds to earthquakes, tides and the injected fluid.

properties.name: OSMO-sampler
properties.description: Collects small samples of the fluid in the borehole over time, to be analysed after it is recovered.

properties.name: Ferry Box
properties.note: Mounted on the CORK wellhead (Geochemistry Sampling Bay B)
properties.description: A sensor package that measures the chemistry of the borehole fluid, here with a CTD, a carbon meter and a fluorometer.
